rounds.q: How many days of school a year do most US states require?
rounds.why: Kansas asks for the most, 186 days, while Colorado asks for the fewest, 160.
rounds.src: Pew Research Center, from Education Commission of the States data (2023)
rounds.fun: 180 days is the usual, but Kansas asks for 186 and Colorado just 160!

rounds.q: What % of US 11-year-olds have their own smartphone?
rounds.why: Only 24% of 9-year-olds have one, but by age 17 it's 94%.
rounds.src: Common Sense Media, 2026 Census: Tech and Media Use by Tweens and Teens (2026 data)
rounds.fun: 57% of 11-year-olds have a phone. From 24% at age 9 to 94% at 17. Ring ring!

rounds.q: In 1969, what % of US kids ages 5 to 14 walked or biked to school?
rounds.why: By 2009, only 13% did, and 45% rode to school in the family car.
rounds.src: National Center for Safe Routes to School, How Children Get to School (1969 vs 2009 data)
rounds.fun: Nearly half walked or biked in 1969. By 2009, just 13%. Sneakers, we miss you!

rounds.q: What % of US kids ages 6 to 17 play on a sports team or take sports lessons?
rounds.why: That's about 27.3 million kids, based on a big national survey of parents.
rounds.src: Aspen Institute Project Play, from the National Survey of Children's Health (2023 data)
rounds.fun: Over half of kids play on a team or take lessons, about 27.3 million of them. Go team!

rounds.q: About how many US kids eat a school lunch on a typical school day?
rounds.why: In 2024 alone, US schools served more than 4.8 billion lunches.
rounds.src: USDA FNS, School Lunch participation (FY2025: 29.99 million); USDA ERS for 4.8 billion lunches (FY2024)
rounds.fun: About 30 million lunch trays a day, and over 4.8 billion lunches in a year. Yum!
